newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says adequate water up to year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says adequate water up to year 2000.

text.p: The Philippines said on Thursday there will be adequate water supply in most parts of the country until year 2000.

"There will be adequate water supply for the country up to the year 2000, but urgent steps must be taken to curb pollution and watershed degration, (and to) rationalise water distribution," public works secretary Gregorio Vigilar in a statement.
He said the dependable surface and underground water sources could yield about 975 million cubic metre per day, enough to meet the demand of only 504 million cubic metre per day by year 2000.

He, however, said certain areas such as the central part of the main Luzon island, and some regions in the central Visayas and southern Mindanao islands could experience long-term water shortage due to higher demand.
"Most of these problems have to be resolved through larger investments for water infrastructure, improved efficiency in service delivery and water use," he added.
Under the government programme, about 90 percent of the total population will have been served by year 2000, from only 63 percent in 1995.
